blocks.heading: Distinguishing activity types
blocks.text: To distinguish activities, follow what happens to the resource or product and who receives the output. Extraction differs from transformation; selling to another business differs from selling to the final consumer. A service can support a physical product without itself being manufacturing. These distinctions prevent classifying an enterprise solely from its size, its name or the fact that it earns money.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A fishing operation lands fish; a processor freezes packaged portions; a shop sells them to families. The fishing operation obtains a natural resource, while the processor transforms or prepares it for sale. The shop’s transaction with a family is retailing. A firm buying cartons from the processor and reselling them to shops performs wholesaling. The ownership form could be the same at several stages without changing the activity performed.
